$comment: Layers 2 and 3 of four (ADR 0046). A `standard` namespace is somebody else's vocabulary. Its words are listed here so a console can offer them, and they are NOT authoritative: `defined_by` is, and where the two disagree the standard wins. This is why a pointer's words are never enforced — a name absent from this copy is accepted, because the copy being short of the standard is the likely reading, not the issuer being wrong. A `vaulet` namespace is one nobody else has written down, and only there are we the authority. Layer 4 is an organisation's own namespace and is not listed here at all. `same_as` names the spelling a verifier is likeliest to already read. It points outward, never inward: a register that made the world's words aliases of its own would be readable only by software that had heard of us, which is the one thing a shared vocabulary is for. The five organisation-name words — institution_name in education and finance, employer_name, insurer_name, provider_name — are deliberately NOT merged: one organisation_name on a staff pass and a gym membership reads the same and says nothing about which is which, and the namespace is what tells them apart.

SMART Health Cards does carry FHIR in a credential, but as one whole Bundle in a single JWS claim — all of it discloses or none of it does, which is the opposite of what SD-JWT is for. So the names are ours and the codes are theirs.

namespaces.meaning: Parts of a person's name that no standard for credentials spells.
namespaces.$comment: OpenID Connect Core stops at name, given_name, family_name and middle_name; ISO's mDL and the EUDI PID carry no honorific at all. SCIM (RFC 7643) does — name.honorificPrefix and name.honorificSuffix — and it is a user-provisioning schema rather than a claim vocabulary, so it is cited here and not pointed at. The spelling follows it in snake_case, so somebody mapping between the two has nothing to guess.

claims.name: honorific_prefix
claims.meaning: What comes before the name: Mr, Mrs, Dr, นาย, นาง, นางสาว. On a Thai identity card it is part of the printed name, so a credential that drops it does not match the document.

claims.name: honorific_suffix
claims.meaning: What comes after it: Jr, III, PhD.

namespaces.meaning: The parts of an address below the town that no vocabulary for credentials spells.
namespaces.$comment: OpenID Connect gives street_address, one free-text line for everything before the town, and DIF's Verified Person address adds extendedAddress and unstructuredAddress — catch-alls by another name. A Thai address is eight labelled boxes on every form that asks for one (FundConnext Single Form v3.1 asks for four such addresses), and putting them in one string is throwing away the structure the form already had. Written beside address.* rather than replacing it: locality, region, postal_code and country are OIDC's and stay OIDC's.

The words come from the FundConnext Single Form, which is the form every Thai asset manager uses.

namespaces.meaning: What an intermediary concluded about somebody, and what they declared.
namespaces.$comment: Two kinds of thing in one namespace on purpose: `objective`, `marital_status` and `spouse_name` are what the person said, while `risk_profile`, `experience` and `time_horizon` are a score somebody computed from ten questions, and `pep` is a check somebody ran. The second kind must carry assessed_by (ADR 0012): birthdate is wrong only if it was mistyped, and a risk profile is wrong whenever a different assessor would have concluded differently.

claims.name: objective
claims.meaning: Why they are investing: investment, retirement, tax benefit.

claims.name: risk_profile
claims.meaning: The suitability result. Assessed, never declared — assessed_by says whose.

claims.name: experience
claims.meaning: How much investing they have done, in the assessor's own scale.

claims.name: time_horizon
claims.meaning: How long the money can be left, in the assessor's own scale.

claims.name: pep
claims.meaning: Whether they are a politically exposed person, or close to one. A check somebody ran, not a fact somebody stated.

claims.name: pep_position
claims.meaning: The office held, when pep is true.

claims.name: marital_status
claims.meaning: Single or married, as the form asks it.

claims.name: spouse_name
claims.meaning: The spouse's name, which several account-opening forms require beside the holder's own.

namespaces.meaning: What is printed and encoded on a passport or a national identity card.
namespaces.$comment: ISO/IEC 18013-5 spells every one of these and cannot be borrowed: its namespace is scoped to the mobile driving licence, and writing a passport's number under org.iso.18013.5.1 says the holder has a driving licence they may not have. ICAO 9303 defines the document and declares no claim vocabulary, so there is nothing to point at — the same position as FHIR and the Single Form. Names follow ISO's spelling so a mapping between the two guesses nothing.

claims.name: type
claims.meaning: P for a passport, ID for a national identity card — the MRZ's document code.

claims.name: number
claims.meaning: The document number, as printed.

claims.name: expiry_date
claims.meaning: When the document expires, which is not when a credential made from it does.

claims.name: issue_date
claims.meaning: When it was issued.

claims.name: issuing_country
claims.meaning: Alpha-3 in the MRZ, and recorded as the MRZ has it.

claims.name: issuing_authority
claims.meaning: Who issued it.

claims.name: place_of_birth
claims.meaning: As printed, which is a place name and not an address.

claims.name: national_id
claims.meaning: The personal number some states carry in the MRZ's optional data.

namespaces.meaning: What a face check concluded, which is not a fact about the person.
namespaces.$comment: Every word here is assessed and none is declared, so a credential carrying one carries assessed_by with it (ADR 0012): a birthdate is wrong only if it was mistyped, and a match score is wrong whenever a different assessor would have scored differently. Transaction-bound (ADR 0010) — the verdict is about one attempt, not about a face.

claims.name: matched
claims.meaning: Whether the live face and the document's portrait were judged the same person.

claims.name: score
claims.meaning: How alike, in the assessor's own scale. Comparable only against thresholds from the same assessor.

claims.name: pad_level
claims.meaning: The presentation-attack-detection level the capture met, as iBeta counts levels.

pending.expected: European Health Insurance Card, as an EUDI attestation
pending.$comment: No namespace identifier is recorded because none is published: annex 3 of the ARF carries rulebooks for PID and the mDL, and the mDL's namespace is ISO's, not the EU's. Writing eu.europa.ec.eudi.ehic.1 here would be inventing a standard's name, which is the one thing this file exists to stop. Listed so a console can warn that cover is likely to get a reserved word later, and so nobody adds one from memory.

A ratified DIF specification (October 2025) covering the identity half of every KYC form: name with honorificPrefix, address with a type, identificationEvidence, contactPoint. It cannot be pointed at because it establishes no namespace identifier of its own — it borrows from Schema.org, OpenID Connect and EBSI — and it is camelCase objects where SD-JWT here is flat snake_case. Recorded so the spellings stay convertible and so nobody writes a second word for honorific_prefix.

pending.expected: FundConnext Single Form, for opening a mutual fund account in Thailand
pending.$comment: Prepared by the Stock Exchange of Thailand with the support of the SEC and AIMC, version 3.1 dated 1 June 2022. It is a PDF form and declares no vocabulary, so the words in `income` and `investor` are ours and its field labels are only where they were found. If a machine-readable version is ever published, those become aliases.
